title: Compact Flow Microcard: Per-Model & Per-Route Performance Card Prototype
creator: Ariana Chen
description: Design a compact, embeddable performance microcard that surfaces per-model and per-route key signals (latency distribution, throughput, token counts, and cost breakdown) for use across the Redwood Console. The card is intended to be reusable in list views (endpoints table), route detail pages, rollout sidebars, and exported runbooks. Emphasis: consumable at glance, supports quick drilldowns to detailed charts, and scales to dense dashboards without overwhelming visual noise.
acceptance_criteria: Microcard layout (collapsed / expanded) implemented in Figma with states for empty/error/loading/has-data
Chart specs documented for token-waterfall, latency-violin, and throughput-sparkline with data aggregation rules
Interactions: hover tooltips, tap-to-drill (route -> trace), mini-canary overlay to show rollout cohorts
A11y: color contrast tokens meet WCAG AA, keyboard focus for expand/collapse and drill-in, aria labels for charts
Performance: visual queries defined to use pre-aggregated metrics (1s/10s downsample) to avoid full trace fetch on hover
Handoff: Figma prototype, exportable JSON spec for charting library, and PRD link provided
design_notes: Card anatomy: left column = compact header + model/route title + badges (region, tier). Middle column = three stacked micro-widgets: token-waterfall (top), latency-violin (middle), throughput-sparkline (bottom). Right column = compact cost & error rate badge with overflow menu for actions (open traces, open rollout, open settings).
Collapsed size: 280x96 px; Expanded size: 560x240 px. Collapsed shows p90 latency, tokens-per-request median, throughput sparkline. Expand reveals full waterfall and violin with percentile toggles.

Token Waterfall chart spec: visualization = stacked horizontal bars representing request phases (prompt, generation, post-process). X-axis = cumulative duration (ms). Bar segments = token counts attributed to phase. Aggregation window = 1m by default, fallback to 5m for low-cardinality routes. Percentiles displayed: p50/p90/p99 as vertical markers. Bucket resolution = 10ms for latencies < 500ms, 50ms otherwise. Sampling: 1 request per 10 for cold routes, 1:1 for high-throughput endpoints. Retention/display window = 30 days with zoom presets (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d).

Latency Violin chart spec: visualization = violin per time-slice (hour) when zoomed, otherwise aggregated violin for selected window. Show kernel density estimate of latency distribution with overlaid median and p90 lines. Y-axis = latency ms (log scale optional). Bandwidth parameter = adaptive (Scott's rule) with min smoothing to avoid spiky noise. Tooltip shows sample count, median, p90, p99, and sample period.

Throughput Sparkline spec: visualization = compact sparkline with area under curve, sampling interval = 10s when zoomed <24h, 1m otherwise. Secondary overlay = autoscaled capacity line when dedicated capacity is present. Hover shows exact rps and active GPUs/replicas if available.

Cost attribution mini-waterfall: left = compute (GPU time normalized to token), middle = per-token model cost, right = infra overhead. Unit = cost per 1k tokens; configurable to show absolute or relative. Sources: runtime billing + cost model computed in Optimize service.

Rollout / Canary overlay: when a rollout is active, display a semi-transparent band on the token-waterfall representing cohort distribution; click 'open rollout' to show canary split, error deltas, and quick rollback action (link to ops).

Data contract: microcard should request a compact metrics payload (pre-aggregated JSON) with fields: time_windows[], p50,p90,p99,token_counts_by_phase[], throughput_timeseries[], cost_breakdown{}. Avoid requesting raw traces on initial render.

Performance constraints: maximum 4 concurrent microcards per page by default; for list views we cap refresh interval to 30s. Cards will degrade gracefully to cached data if backend rate-limit encountered.

Accessibility: ensure violin and waterfall have text alternatives summarizing key numbers; allow switching to numeric-only mode for screen readers. Use high-contrast palette for critical deltas (regressions >10% use red/orange).
Theming: support light/dark, small/compact density. Colors chosen to align with Redwood design tokens: token-primary (#0B5FFF), token-warning (#FF8A00), token-danger (#D8262A), token-muted (#6B7280).
feedback: PM (Elliot): prioritize p90 prominently, but keep p50 visible to surface shifts in majority user experience.
Eng (Sana): backend will expose pre-aggregated waterfall segments; ensure bucketization matches runtime's token-phase boundaries to avoid mismatch.
Research (Jon): consider adding a 'token-cost delta' spark when model quantization is toggled in Optimize; useful for linking cost anomalies to model variants.
Design lead (Maya): reduce vertical padding in collapsed state to keep lists compact; prefer left-aligned header to improve scanability.
Accessibility reviewer (Priya): request keyboard-only prototype to validate focus order; include aria-live region for realtime alerts (e.g., error spike).
